samples.summary: The session-start reconcile destroys the archive of every document that was deleted upstream — the exact unsent work the recovery offer exists to hand back — before the offer is ever made.
samples.evidence: `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments()` enumerates `storedDocumentIds({ archives: true })` and, for every id not in the server listing, calls `purgeDocument(id, { archives: "drop", skipOpen: true, updatedSince: listedAt })` (offline-erase.ts:487-497). "The document was deleted or GC'd upstream" is one of the three documented causes of an archive (offline-copy.ts header), and `GET /documents` hard-deletes (`document.service.ts:126 prisma.document.delete`), so such an id can never be in `accessible`. `dropArchivesForDocument` only spares rows with `archivedAt >= updatedSince` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1031-1036) — an archive written in a *previous* session always fails that — or rows whose document is open, which a deleted document never is. And `OfflineRuntime` runs the reconcile strictly *before* `offerRecoverableWork` (offline-runtime.tsx:157 then 192), and offers only once per mount, so an archive created mid-session is first offered next session, by which time the reconcile has already deleted it. This directly contradicts the deliberate exemption on the same path: `purgeOfflineDocuments` defaults to `archives: "keep"` precisely because "'deleted upstream' is one of the three paths that produce an archive" (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:886-889). Net effect: the only durable copy of work the server never took is silently deleted, which is the loss the feature exists to prevent.

samples.summary: On the currently pinned build the chip tells every user with unsent work "This browser cannot save documents locally" — a build-time library check reported as a browser capability.
samples.evidence: `lapse` is computed as `!supportsClientKey() ? "unsupported" : ...` (collab-document-provider.tsx:291-299), and `supportsClientKey()` reads `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__` against `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` (yorkie-capabilities.ts). `packages/frontend/package.json:66` pins `@yorkie-js/react` at `0.7.22`, so the predicate is false on every build shipped by this PR. The scope wraps both branches and the editor subtree, and `SyncStatusChip` renders inside it (document-detail.tsx:910-921 → SiteHeader → SyncStatusChip), so `tooltipFor(...)` appends `LAPSE_REASONS.unsupported` = "This browser cannot save documents locally." to the `not-saved` tooltip for *every* user who goes offline today — including on the share route, where the correct reason is `not-permitted`. The statement is false (it is the app build, not the browser) and it is on the commonest path the chip has.

samples.summary: The per-document `WafflebaseDocStore` built in `DurableYorkieProvider`'s `useMemo` is never closed, leaking one IndexedDB connection per document opened.
samples.evidence: `const store = useMemo(() => new WafflebaseDocStore({...}), [userId])` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:148-189) has no companion `useEffect` returning `store.close()`; a grep for `store.close` finds it only in `offline-runtime.tsx:208` and `offline-erase.ts`. Every navigation between documents unmounts this provider and constructs a new store, so open connections accumulate for the life of the tab. `WafflebaseDocStore.close()` exists precisely because a held connection blocks `deleteDatabase`/version upgrades elsewhere (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:532).

samples.summary: `close()` called while `open()` is still in flight leaves the connection open and re-attaches it to the supposedly closed store.
samples.evidence: `close()` does `this.db?.close(); this.db = undefined; this.opening = undefined;` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:533-537). If the open request has not yet fired `onsuccess`, `this.db` is still undefined, so nothing is closed; when the pending `request.onsuccess` later runs it executes `this.db = db; resolve(db)` (lines 509-521), leaving a live IDBDatabase on a store the caller believes it released. `OfflineRuntime`'s cleanup (offline-runtime.tsx:208) can reach exactly this ordering, because the effect's async body starts `retryPendingOfflineErase()`/`collectStale()` — which open the database — and unmount can land before the open resolves.

samples.summary: Switching the preference off and back on inside one session orphans everything the still-mounted durable client writes afterwards, because the client-key salt was rotated underneath it.
samples.evidence: `eraseOfflineData()` calls `forgetDeviceSecret(userId)` (offline-erase.ts:39), which deletes the per-document salts so the next `durableClientKey()` mints a new one (durable-session.ts:270-300). The durable client is deliberately left mounted across the preference change (`collab-document-provider.tsx` holds the decision for the life of the open document; `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:185` only gates writes). If the preference is re-enabled in the same session, `isPersistenceEnabled()` is true again and the SDK resumes writing under the *old* `clientKey`, while any later page load derives a *different* key — so the SDK's `apiKey/clientKey/docKey` scope no longer matches and none of that work can be resumed; it sits unreachable until the thirty-day sweep.

samples.summary: An identity change under an open durable editor returns `null`, unmounting the `DocumentProvider` and discarding the in-memory change queue — the teardown the surrounding comments say must never happen.
samples.evidence: `if (!ready && held.current?.subject !== subject) return null;` (line 333). `subject` embeds `person?.id` (line 256), and a React Query refetch that resolves a *different* user changes it; `useDurableDocument` then resets its `latched` ref and reports `answered === false`, so `settled` is false for the new subject (use-durable-document.ts:166-171, 232, 254). `ready` is therefore false while `held.current.subject !== subject`, the guard fires, and the whole editor subtree under `inner` unmounts — discarding the Yorkie change queue the file's own comments (lines 200-209, 322-328) identify as the loss this feature exists to prevent.

samples.summary: The `wafflebase-offline-denied` list grows without bound and is only ever pruned for an account that signs in again on this device.
samples.evidence: `denyOfflineWrites` appends to the stored array on every deliberate sign-out (offline-erase.ts:186-189) and `permitOfflineWrites` removes an id only from `rememberOfflineUser` on a later sign-in (lines 75-82). On a shared device each distinct account that signs out and never returns leaves a permanent entry, and `isOfflineWritePermitted` JSON-parses the whole list on every single store write (line 208-213).

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out against the repo. offline-erase.ts:487-497 enumerates stored ids including archives and calls purgeDocument(id, {archives:"drop", skipOpen:true, updatedSince:listedAt}) for any id absent from the server listing. "Deleted or GC'd upstream" is a documented archive cause (offline-copy.ts:9-13) and the backend hard-deletes (document.service.ts:129, :139), so such an id can never appear in fetchDocuments(). dropArchivesForDocument spares a row only when archivedAt >= updatedSince or the docKey is live (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1031-1037) — an archive from a prior session and a deleted document satisfy neither. OfflineRuntime runs the reconcile (offline-runtime.tsx:154-161) strictly before the single, mount-scoped offer (offline-runtime.tsx:192, 229; effect deps [userId] at :210), so a mid-session archive spared by listedAt is deleted by the next session's reconcile before it is ever offered. This contradicts the same file's deliberate archives:"keep" default rationale (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:886-889) and renders the offer path's explicit 404 "deleted upstream" fallback (offline-runtime.tsx:264-278) effectively dead. Result is silent loss of the only copy of work the server never took — critical data loss, squarely in the correctness lane.

verdict.reason: Verified end to end. package.json:66 pins @yorkie-js/react at 0.7.22; vite.config.ts:414-418 injects that pin as __YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__; yorkie-capabilities.ts:24,44-57,76-82 makes supportsClientKey() false for 0.7.22 vs MinClientKeyVersion 0.7.23. collab-document-provider.tsx:291-299 therefore yields lapse === "unsupported" for every non-durable document (which is all of them on this build, since mayPersist at :223 is false), and that branch is tested before !permitted, so it also masks "not-permitted" on the share route (shared-document.tsx:1017,1093 wraps in NonDurableScope). The lapse scope wraps both branches (:350-373) and the chip renders inside it (document-detail.tsx:910-921 -> site-header.tsx:108; shared-header-status.tsx:26). SyncStatusChip reads useDurabilityLapse() (sync-status-chip.tsx:79) and passes it to tooltipFor (:322), which appends LAPSE_REASONS.unsupported = "This browser cannot save documents locally." (sync-status-tooltip.ts:30,111-112) to the not-saved tooltip. No guard suppresses it — the only supportsClientKey() check in the chip gates offerOffline (:95-99). Result: a false cause shown to every user with unsent work on a reachable path, and a wrong reason precedence on the share route. Real and blocking under the correctness rubric.
